name: Drawing Toys
description: Two small drawing machines: an unbroken line steered by twin dials, and a soft magnetic board with movable stamps and a sliding eraser.

assets.credit: Original twin-dial and magnetic toy illustration

compatibility: Canvas 2D and Pointer Events; no runtime dependencies, image requests, fonts or audio.
Captured mouse, trackpad and touch gestures. Keyboard arrows and direction buttons provide alternate input. Drawing surfaces reserve touch gestures; the surrounding page scrolls normally.
Animation rests offscreen, in hidden tabs and when paused. Reduced motion removes the shake and animated wipe; deliberate replay remains available.
The board retains normalized paths when its proportions change. Up to 16,000 semantic marks per toy and 24 undo gestures bound memory use.
notes: An original molded red twin-dial shell and a rounded porcelain magnetic shell have separate drawing documents. Their naming and decoration are original, without copied logos or branded artwork.

The twin-dial head cannot lift. Circular knob movement changes one axis, center dragging gives a linear alternative, and dragging the screen moves the existing head by a relative displacement. Repositioning a pointer cannot teleport the line.

The magnetic surface uses a cached fine cell texture and soft gray marks. Lift the stylus for separate strokes; drag stamps or select one and tap. The sliding eraser removes only the strip it crosses, in either direction.

Shake the top grip back and forth, or press Shake to erase. The board tilts and its line fades before the clear commits. A full magnetic sweep moves across the actual drawing. Undo restores either gesture.
Replay is generated from stored line, stamp and wipe events. Scrubbing backward reconstructs the earlier image, including earlier eraser operations. New edits return to the completed drawing.
reuse: Use mount(host, settings) for the complete instrument. It returns update, setRunning, replay, serialize, loadPath, getState and dispose.
The independent model stores normalized drawing data; input.js maps pointers/keys into that model; renderer.js caches paper and ink; erase.js supplies sampled erase poses; export.js produces PNGs.
Serve the exported source over HTTP. example.html includes the complete toy; embed-demo.html shows a small independent board using only the model and renderer.
Drawing JSON includes artwork and erase events. Lab presets contain appearance/interaction settings, not the current visitor artwork. Path imports use an array of [x,y] points, each from zero to one.
